These are going to conflict with the existing platform init for gb200.  Please look and make sure that we have a process for initting ONLY the GPu card.  Those logical things should go into the GPU process if needed, because they're not platform specific.

I've made some improvements:
1) Platform init is performed via the existing gb200 service.
2) Not doing restart of the FRU service anymore.
3) Steps are specific to card init.
Looking much cleaner
Please don't do this on new scripts.  You've just subverted the whole point of running shellcheck.

I've fixed the issues reported by SC2006.

However, SC2046 is required as it disallows the way gpioset is used with gpiofind due to the warning suggesting using quotes, which wouldn't work with the way gpiofind is used here. This check is disabled in several other scripts in openbmc for the same reason.
What does this do for you?
This wasn't required and has been removed. It was to just check what the FRU service reported. The sleeps have been mostly eliminated as well.

Answering patricks question, at one point there was a Naive dts that didn't wait to bring up the i2c busses after power had been asserted, and this was a heavy-handed kludge to make fru device rescan.  The DTS being moved through lkml now has that fixed.
I guess these are things you can choose to do, but I don't know why you would restart mctpd.
This has been fixed.
Done

This should be done in the MCTP dbus-sensors daemon, right?

https://github.com/openbmc/dbus-sensors/tree/master/src/mctp

There is some precedence here for doing this in the meta layer (until we can get the EM schema for static endpoint assignment through). See https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/a1a140c2a1b6ab09b729a3138e8d5e05a6200541/meta-facebook/meta-yosemite4/recipes-phosphor/gpio/phosphor-gpio-monitor/configure-nic-mctp-endpoint#L19, for example.
ACK, I didn't realize this was initting the bmc itself.  Leave a comment to that effect, then this is fine.
Added a comment.
Done
Lets try to avoid multi-second sleeps in any startup code.  If there's a known reason to do it, leave a comment, but there shouldn't be any hardware that actually takes 5 seconds to init.
This has been removed.
Done

????  No.  Platform init is intentionally the only owners of those GPIOs to avoid conflicts.  If you want to manipulate them after platform init, add more handling into the platform-init daemon.

Regardless of that, we're not going to randomly kill system services.
Moved to platform init daemon.
Done
This is going to put the system in HMC+BMC mode.  That's not correct.  ANy idea why this was needed?

On the platform that I am testing the PCIe card, there is an HMC. Setting this causes the HMC to get USB connectivity to the MCU instead of the BMC.

When this is not set, the following is as expected:

root@gb200nvl-obmc:~# lsusb
unable to initialize usb specBus 001 Device 001: ID 1d6b:0002 Linux 6.6.90-5a4c983-dirty-64c9503-00419-g64c9503f0460 ehci_hcd EHCI Host Controller
Bus 001 Device 002: ID 0424:2422  
Bus 001 Device 009: ID 0525:a4a2 Linux 6.6.58-b2c3c09-19283-gb2c3c09cc992 with aspeed-udc RNDIS/Ethernet Gadget
Bus 001 Device 010: ID 0424:2517  
Bus 001 Device 011: ID 10c4:ea71 Silicon Labs CP2108 Quad USB to UART Bridge Controller
Bus 001 Device 012: ID 0955:cf11  
Bus 002 Device 001: ID 1d6b:0001 Linux 6.6.90-5a4c983-dirty-64c9503-00419-g64c9503f0460 uhci_hcd Generic UHCI Host Controller



When this is set, the BMC doesn't see the MCU:

root@gb200nvl-obmc:~# gpioset $(gpiofind HMC_BMC_DETECT-O)=1  
root@gb200nvl-obmc:~# lsusb
unable to initialize usb specBus 001 Device 001: ID 1d6b:0002 Linux 6.6.90-5a4c983-dirty-64c9503-00419-g64c9503f0460 ehci_hcd EHCI Host Controller
Bus 001 Device 002: ID 0424:2422  
Bus 001 Device 009: ID 0525:a4a2 Linux 6.6.58-b2c3c09-19283-gb2c3c09cc992 with aspeed-udc RNDIS/Ethernet Gadget
Bus 002 Device 001: ID 1d6b:0001 Linux 6.6.90-5a4c983-dirty-64c9503-00419-g64c9503f0460 uhci_hcd Generic UHCI Host Controller
Why sleep 1 inbetween each of these?  There's no setup time for the gpio expander.
This has been removed - moved to gpio mux.
This is a gpio mux.  Can we please use the appropriate drivers for it?  If we want to, we can still bind them here (or in the platform-init.cpp ideally)
Moved to gpio mux

This is already done in platform_init.  If the location and timing of that reset needs rearranged, please rearrange it there https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/master/meta-nvidia/meta-gb200nvl-obmc/recipes-nvidia/platform-init/files/platform_init.cpp#L162
Moved to platform init daemon.
Done
Should be done in the mctp EM reactor, right?

No, MCTP local address assignment is not handled by mctp reactor/mctpd. There is precedence here already where a platform script does it. For example:

https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/master/meta-facebook/meta-catalina/recipes-networking/mctp/files/setup-local-eid#L23
